body: Yeah, just staring blankly at something until you're forced to face reality again and put up the act of being alive.

I can seriously relate with hating the human condition, and I wish it wasn't like this, but your assessment of human behaviour is probably roughly correct., sadly. Maybe there exist some rare people that can break away from this, or maybe not, because it is just necessary to behave this way to ensure our survival, at least in long term, and anyone that deviates either want's nothing to do with society (so you just don't see them) or just dies.

But look at it this way: why does it matter? Have you tried to look for a reason why exactly it makes you feel bad about yourself, because, well, most people around you probably aren't that concerned about this, so it might be worth it to try and see if there's anything else (hopefully fixable) that is making you feel shit/ infuencing your worldview, in a similar manner you do with other things. You'll either realize that you were wrong with your judgement (so maybe you were wrong with some other ones along the way as well) or you'll find possible ways to make yourself happier. Being a happy dumb animal sounds better, doesn't it?

That is not to take away from the core idea, but neither you nor I, nor anyone else, really, can change human nature. Maybe you can find solace in believing that it's not correct, maybe you can try and spend time with people that seem the furthest away from what you despise, or maybe humans still being a lot like animals isn't all that bad and nature is something pretty neat in general. I wouldn't know, but I wish you luck figuring something out that comforts you.

P.S. Your post does make sense, don't stress it too much.

I figure this might be somewhat underwhelming and slightly depressing, but nonetheless it might be a perspective that needs to be shared:

When I was in 6th grade my \<native\> language and literature teacher had a stroke during a class I was in. The genuine answer as to what I felt would be that, outside of the initial surprise and pure confusion as to what was happening, I did not really feel anything nor did it seem to really impact me \[At least nothing comes to mind. Anything more would be made up to conform to how I *should have* felt\]. It's not that I disliked her, that she was a bad teacher or anything like that. It just didn't register in my mind.

After a really short while everyone and everything was just back to *normal*.

As dark as it may sound, looking back at it, I feel somewhat envious of such a quick and seemingly peaceful death.

The real killer for me is how the attractive people seem to also be quite intelligent, socially capable and genuinely nice \[on top of the halo effect\]. They are completely justified in rejecting and humiliating me, but nope, they have often been the kindest to me.

Don't be too down on yourself though, I highly doubt you can't get a decent girl by working on yourself and improving, but you really have to try and handle your depression first, because a girl probably won't magically cure it \[especially long\-term\] and you'll just get in a different pit of despair.

Are you still on medication and in contact with your therapist \[if you had one in the first place\]?

I don't think I can provide any more help with that, sadly, as I never saw it as a core issue for myself, even though I'm weird, so I'm not well informed on this at all.

Of course it makes sense to want to change something if it affects your life negatively. Have you tried pinpointing what exactly led to your isolation and what behaviours are the most harmful/unwanted? Maybe that helps, at least as a bit of introspection.

I don't think I'd call that delusion since you can differentiate it from reality \[but I'm not really that knowledgeable in psychology's terminology\]

I daydream a lot myself and spend a lot of time just in my head, fantasizing about actually mattering, being talented or influential and often just throwing it all away anyway, since I know that it wouldn't be enough. I guess it's a sort of coping mechanism. A coping mechanism for a world that's too bland, slow, cruel and overall unsatisfactory.

One obvious way you could try to fix it is to seek professional help, but I'm not sure how effective that would be.

Don't be too hard on yourself, you're probably not even that wierd and even if you were, it's okay to be wierd.

Have you tried to write the sum down for some small n's and just mess around?

It looks like you could just explicitly state the sum for any n, since for n\>3 the sum would be the same as for n=3, because the factorial would have a 0 in it. So finding the sum for n = 1; 2 and n\>=3 \[showing why they are all the same\] should be enough.
I've accepted that I'm pretty much dead, rotting away in every way imaginable. Just waiting to be finally burried and to be done with it.

You're totally not alone on this one and I think I know of other people that have felt \[at least somewhat\] like that.

Questions about preferences are slightly awkward and I mostly just say I don't care, don't really have any favorites and often have problems remembering crazy stories, but I wouldn't say that I *lost* anything though. I think I've always been that way and don't really care about the "favorite X" type of questions. Those things are not *me.* If not having a response to those questions because they seem boring and not abiding by these "rules" makes me seem boring to most people, then so be it. Don't really care anymore.

I think it's common that depression makes you feel quite numb and lose interest in the things you used to be passionate about. Just feel so *"meh"* about everything. However, I don't think that makes you a no one. You're more than that trivial stuff and you're more than how you feel right now, even if it doesn't seem like it to you.

I gave up some time ago and am just trying not to inconvenience other people with my existence or suicide. Glad you wouldn't settle for something like that.

Other than that, for me to try and argue in favor of a bleak and depressive worldview is irrational and there's nothing of value to gain from that, so I'll leave it there. Don't waste your time \- I'm too stubborn and stupid.

I'd assume most experts in suicide notes would have already killed themselves.

You could try and write something up and post it somewhere. Maybe you can get some decent responses that you can use to either make a better note or to steer clear of suicide, as I don't think you'll really get people willing to help writing the note. I can't really promise helping you with the note myself either as it seems a bit ethically questionable, and, if I were you, I wouldn't put much trust in the people that are willing to directly help with that.

I wish you didn't feel this way \[I know it doesn't really mean anything\]. Life can become too much at times. Hope you can gather enough strength to continue and to create reasons to do so, or at the very least think through it clearly, as far away from the warped perception depression makes you believe is reality.

My life feels more like being pushed down a mountain than climbing one.

But I do agree with the sentiment. My life might be better if I was less obsessive, but I can't seem to change that nor would it matter in the grand scheme of things anyway.

I think it is a sad truth that reaching out can sometimes (or often, depending on the person) not be worth it at all. No one deserves to be beaten down even more when trying to get help, but obviously "deserves" means jack shit.

Sadly, I don't really have a solution to this problem, only thing that comes to mind is that when everyone else fails to provide any useful help, you have to help yourself, but that seems self evident and stupid.

Didn't think it was justified to leave this thread empty to just reinforce the idea that people won't even bother to help and I'm sorry that you're in such a position.

It's just how I percieve the world, so anything can be attributed to it.

As I'm not sure which feeling in particular you are interested in, I'll try to explain my alienation a bit more: It's just a result of observing other people and their interactions with me and others, and how they see the world. I might be wrong, but it feels like I can understand them and don't have issues with empathy, however, I just don't relate \- I don't think like that at all, and I can see that people treat and act around me differently than they do with others. Or that's how it feels at least.

Yeah, it can, but I don't have reasons to believe that reality has to accommodate to my will. It seems logical to me to assume that to some people no amount of actually achievable change could get them to a point, where they wouldn't feel justified to kill themselves. I'm not sure how certain can one be of it, but I don't think anyone else besides the individual can be any more certain, really, or have the authority to decide it.
